title: Implementation Consultant III, Enterprise Hotels and Sports + Entertainment
description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.
 A day in the life 
 As an Implementation Consultant III, you architect complex technical setups and lead high-stakes, multi-location rollouts for Enterprise clients. Leveraging deep expertise in Toast's technology suite, configurations, content hierarchies, and integration frameworks for multi-site operations.
 Your day might start with a working session with a brand's corporate IT team to map network requirements across multiple locations, move into a hierarchy that a franchisee can update without breaking corporate brand standards, and end with unblocking a peer on a tricky hardware escalation. You move fluidly between the technical detail and the executive conversation — one moment troubleshooting an integration, the next reframing a rollout timeline for a regional VP.
 You are a leader on the Technical Onboarding team. You mentor peers, spot workflow gaps before they become fire drills, and serve as the primary escalation point when advanced hardware and software challenges surface across the Enterprise deployment organization.
 What you'll do (Responsibilities) 
 Architect complex technical setups and design scalable configurations for multi-site operations
 Lead high-stakes, multi-location rollouts for Enterprise brands from design through go-live
 Lead integration frameworks that hold up across dozens or hundreds of sites
 Independently manage intricate franchisee and corporate relationships, proactively mitigating brand-level risks before they surface
 Act as the primary escalation point for resolving advanced hardware, software, and networking challenges
 Lead cross-functional initiatives and drive project success across the Enterprise deployment organization
 Partner with Integrations, Product, and Sales to remove blockers for large brands
 Provide internal QA for multi-unit rollouts, catching configuration issues before they reach the customer
 Mentor peers, identify workflow gaps, and present viable solutions that scale beyond a single project
 What you'll need to thrive (Requirements) 
 5+ years of combined experience in POS, technology, or SaaS
 Familiarity with POS device installation and troubleshooting - onsite or remote 
 Demonstrated experience implementing complex hardware and software at scale, managing integrations, and applying advanced networking skills
 A master understanding of corporate IT and operational needs, with comfort working directly with corporate IT leaders and regional managers
 Advanced understanding of Enterprise configurations, above-store reporting, and third-party integrations 
 Proven ability to own and drive cross-team escalations to resolution
 Project management strength that requires no oversight — you improve Enterprise procedures on your own initiative and complete complex, multi-phased rollouts start to finish
 Impeccable judgment on complex corporate issues, with ownership of missteps without management prompting
 A self-starter's instinct for navigating multi-unit chaos and bringing structure to it
 Confidence building cross-functional relationships and influencing successful multi-team collaboration
 Leadership by example — a scalable mindset and a consistent willingness to help peers navigate complex multi-unit configurations
 Willingness to travel to various customer locations
 What will help you stand out (Non-essential Skills/Nice to Haves) 
 Experience with various customers within the Enterprise, Hotels, Sports, and Entertainment industry
 Proven experience operating in fast-paced, high-volume restaurants, hotels, sports and/or entertainment venue environments.
 Strong understanding of POS systems and restaurant operations workflows, or experience supporting multi-unit QSR or fast casual brands.
 AI at Toast 
 At Toast, one of our company values is that we're hungry to build and learn. We believe learning new AI tools empowers us to build for our customers faster, more independently, and with higher quality. We provide these tools across all disciplines, from Engineering and Product to Sales and Support, and are inspired by how our Toasters are already driving real value with them. The people who thrive here are those who embrace changes that let us build more for our customers; it's a core part of our culture.
 Our Total Rewards Philosophy 
 We strive to provide competitive compensation and benefits programs that help to attract, retain, and motivate the best and brightest people in our industry. Our total rewards package goes beyond great earnings potential and provides the means to a healthy lifestyle with the flexibility to meet Toasters' changing needs. Learn more about our benefits at https://careers.toasttab.com/toast-benefits .
 The base salary range for this role is listed below. The starting salary will be determined based on skills, experience, and geographic location. In addition to base salary, our total rewards components include cash compensation (overtime, bonus/commissions if eligible), equity, and benefits. You can learn more about how we align pay with local labor markets in our Geographic Pay Zone Philosophy . 
 Zone A
 $93,000 — $149,000 USD 
 Zone B
 $81,000 — $130,000 USD 
 Zone C
 $73,000 — $117,000 USD 
 How Toast Uses AI in its Hiring Process 
 Throughout the hiring process, our goal is to get to know you. We use AI tools to support our recruiters and interviewers with tasks like note-taking, summarization, and documentation of interviews to ensure they can be fully focused on your conversation. All hiring decisions are made by people. We ask that you complete interviews and assessments on your own, without real-time AI tools, recording, or transcription bots, unless we tell you otherwise in advance. To learn more: https://careers.toasttab.com/ai-in-hiring 
 Our Approach to Hybrid Working 
We embrace a hybrid work mode

title: Customer Success Manager, Mid-Market
location: New York, NY (HQ) / San Francisco, CA USA
salary_text: $142K – $216K • Offers Equity • 70/30 split on salary and variable compensation
description:
ABOUT RAMP

Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books.

The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving.

We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome.

The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same.

If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Ramp's Mid-Market Customer Success Managers on the Lifecycle team don't stop at go-live — they make sure customers keep getting more from Ramp as their business grows. Ramp has grown its product suite significantly over the last several years. As we've matured as an organization, our customer relationships have grown more complex too: customers are buying more of the platform at once, running it across more entities and teams, and relying on it for more of how their finance function operates. Hitting an activation milestone doesn't mean the job's finished. Too often, a feature that could solve a real problem goes unused because no one is there to show how it would work in that customer's business.

That's where you come in. This is a role for people who understand how finance teams actually run, who think in years rather than quarters, and who already use AI the way surgeons use instruments: not occasionally, not as an experiment, but as the default way they work. You'll own the customer experience after implementation for a book of mid-market customers, partnering with Account Management on long-term account strategy. You'll also be one of the first Lifecycle CSMs on a newly formed team, helping define how Ramp earns and keeps the trust of its customers.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 1.  Own the post-implementation experience for a book of mid-market customers, with clear accountability for sustained adoption, customer satisfaction, and renewal readiness

 2.  Drive sustained adoption by understanding each customer's goals and guiding them toward the workflows that improve outcomes for their business — including the products and features they've already purchased but haven't fully put to work

 3.  Act as each customer's expert in finance workflows: understand how they run their business, advise on decisions as their needs change, and make the value of new Ramp capabilities clear in their context

 4.  Build multi-threaded relationships in every account, including finance leadership relationships you own, so the account stays steady through change like a new Controller or CFO

 5.  Partner with Account Management on QBRs and business reviews, quantifying Ramp's impact in the language CFOs and Controllers care about — close cycle improvement, spend visibility, savings, and ROI — not just product usage metrics

 6.  Spot opportunities for growth and bring them to Account Management, who owns renewals and expansion; as customers add products, drive ongoing activation so they reach value quickly

 7.  Run your book on data: monitor usage, CP, and risk signals, prioritize where your time goes, and get ahead of challenges and escalations before they reach renewal

 8.  Use AI tools daily to prepare for customer calls, build materials, synthesize data, identify account risk, and operate at a pace traditional methods can't match

 9.  Bring customer feedback back into Ramp — surfacing patterns, gaps, and opportunities from your accounts to shape how Ramp evolves

 10. Turn what works into repeatable plays, programs, and automations that scale across your book and the team




WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - 5+ years of customer-facing experience in customer success, account management, or consulting, with a proven, consistent track record of retaining customers and exceeding goals

 - Experience owning a book of customers past launch and through renewal, with measurable retention, adoption, or satisfaction results; finance or fintech context is a plus but not required

 - A customer experience mindset — you get ahead of problems before customers raise them and own escalations through resolution

 - AI fluency as a daily habit — you already use AI tools habitually to prep for calls, synthesize information, build customer-facing materials, and automate repetitive tasks; this is how you work, not something you're exploring

 - Ability to communicate Ramp's impact in financial terms — walking a Controller through the value Ramp has delivered and connecting adoption to P&L outcomes

 - A data-driven approach to managing a book — you prioritize based on usage, revenue, and risk signals and can spot an at-risk account well before renewal

 - Technical and systems acumen to understand how Ramp fits into a customer's finance stack, diagnose what's blocking adoption, and bring in the right technical partner

 - A builder mindset — this team is new, and you're energized by shaping the playbooks, programs, and rituals that define how Lifecycle CSMs work while running your own book; you bring structure to ambiguity and iterate quickly

 - Strong collaboration and influencing skills across Sales, Account Management, Product, Operations, and other GTM teams




NICE TO HAVES

 1. Experience with a consumption-based product where value is measured in usage or spend, not seats

 2. Exposure to FP&A, accounting software ecosystems (NetSuite, Sage, QuickBooks, Xero), expense management, or CFO-adjacent workflows

 3. Demonstrated commercial impact — retention, adoption, or renewal outcomes

 As a Customer Support Specialist - Risk, you’ll be part of a team dedicated to managing customer interactions and operational tasks across key risk-related workstreams. You’ll collaborate with multiple Risk teams at Mercury, including AML, Fraud, ODD, Onboarding, Sanctions, and Risk UX, to provide clear, thoughtful, and accurate support to customers impacted by risk-related decisions or processes.
 Your work is operational in nature, focused on handling inbound customer communications, managing requests efficiently, and ensuring that our customers have an excellent experience even in sensitive or complex situations.
 This is a fincrime-oriented , CX-first operational support role that connects the customer experience to Mercury’s internal risk infrastructure.
 What You’ll Do 
 Serve as the first point of contact for customers impacted by risk actions (e.g., account restrictions, closures, or other reviews)
 Manage inbound email inquiries related to:
 Account restrictions or closures initiated by Risk
 Legal, physical, or residential address updates
 Check disbursement or reissuance requests

 Act as the primary internal point of contact for Risk teams when updates or process changes may impact Customer Support workflows

 Work operationally day-to-day, prioritizing accuracy, empathy, and timeliness in all communications

 Foundational understanding of what “risk” means in a fintech context, and how Risk teams work together to mitigate and manage it

 Excellent English reading and writing skills; highly comfortable handling written communications in a sensitive context
